kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-01.title: Take away one bar
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-01.body:
Four bars minus one bar is three bars, and that difference is 6 EUR. So three bars cost 6 EUR and one bar costs $6 \div 3 = 2$ EUR.

**Answer: (B) 2 EUR**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-01.title: Equation
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-01.body:
Let one bar cost $x$. Then $4x = x + 6$, so $3x = 6$ and $x = 2$.

**Answer: (B) 2 EUR**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-02.title: Read carefully
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-02.body:
How far you can see depends on the height of the lighthouse, not on how many kangaroos are looking. Each of the 10 kangaroos still sees 5 km.

**Answer: (A) 5 km**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-08.title: Is Alice telling the truth?
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-08.body:
If Alice told the truth, today would be Monday – but on Mondays Alice lies. Contradiction. So Alice is lying: today is **not** Monday, and it is one of Alice's lying days, i.e. Wednesday or Thursday.

Bob says Alice's false statement is true, so Bob is lying too. Bob lies on Thursday, Friday, Sunday.

The only day in both lists is Thursday.

**Answer: (E) Thursday**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-08.title: Test the options
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-08.body:
- Friday: Alice tells the truth, so she wouldn't say "Monday". ✗
- Sunday: Alice tells the truth. ✗
- Monday: Alice lies, so she wouldn't truthfully say "Monday". ✗
- Wednesday: Alice lies ✓, but Bob tells the truth on Wednesday and would not confirm a false statement. ✗
- Thursday: Alice lies ✓ and Bob lies ✓.

**Answer: (E) Thursday**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-13.title: Count rows and columns
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-13.body:
Suppose $a$ cuts are parallel to one side and $b$ to the other, $a + b = 7$. The cuts make $a+1$ strips one way and $b+1$ the other, so

$$N = (a+1)(b+1), \qquad (a+1) + (b+1) = 9.$$

Possible products: $1\cdot8 = 8$, $2\cdot7 = 14$, $3\cdot6 = 18$, $4\cdot5 = 20$.

12 cannot be obtained.

**Answer: (B) 12**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-13.title: Check 12 directly
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-13.body:
To get 12 pieces as a grid we would need $(a+1)(b+1) = 12$ with $(a+1)+(b+1) = 9$. The factor pairs of 12 are $1\cdot12$, $2\cdot6$, $3\cdot4$ with sums 13, 8, 7 – never 9.

**Answer: (B) 12**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-15.title: Multiply the factors
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-15.body:
A discount of 10% multiplies the price by 0.9, 20% by 0.8, 30% by 0.7.

- A-cell: $100 \cdot 0.9 \cdot 0.8 \cdot 0.7 = 50.40$
- B-cell: $100 \cdot 0.8 \cdot 0.8 \cdot 0.8 = 51.20$
- C-cell: $100 \cdot 0.7 \cdot 0.9 \cdot 0.8 = 50.40$

A-cell and C-cell use the same three factors (order doesn't matter in multiplication), and they are cheaper than B-cell.

**Answer: (D) A-cell and C-cell**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-15.title: Compare without the full calculation
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-15.body:
A and C apply the same discounts in a different order, so they end at the same price. Compare $0.9 \cdot 0.7 = 0.63$ with $0.8 \cdot 0.8 = 0.64$ (both also have one factor 0.8): A and C are slightly cheaper than B.

**Answer: (D) A-cell and C-cell**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-24.title: Find a plan with two turns
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-24.body:
**Turn 1** at time 0: all three glasses start running.

At minute 4 the 4-minute glass is empty. The 3-minute glass has been empty since minute 3 (all its sand is at the bottom).

**Turn 2** at minute 4: now the 3-minute glass has all its sand on top again and runs for exactly 3 more minutes – it empties at minute $4 + 3 = 7$.

So 7 minutes are measured from the first turn until the 3-minute glass runs out.

**One turn is not enough:** after a single turn the only moments you can observe are when a glass runs out – minutes 3, 4 and 5. None of them is 7.

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-24.title: Check every possible second turn
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-24.body:
After the first turn, the only moments we can recognise are when a glass runs out: minutes 3, 4 and 5. So the second turn must happen at one of them.

- Turn at minute 3: each glass then has exactly 3 minutes of sand on top (3-glass: all 3; 4-glass: 3 of 4 already fell; 5-glass: 3 of 5 already fell), so all run out at minute 6.
- Turn at minute 4: the 3-glass restarts and runs out at minute **7**. ✓
- Turn at minute 5: the glasses run out at minutes 8, 9 and 10.

Only turning at minute 4 works, and it uses 2 turns.

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-27.title: Work modulo 120°
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-27.body:
An equilateral triangle rotated about its centre by $120^\circ$ covers the same region. So only the total angle modulo $120^\circ$ matters.

Total angles after each step: $0^\circ, 3^\circ, 12^\circ, 39^\circ, 120^\circ, \dots$

After 4 steps the total is $3 + 9 + 27 + 81 = 120^\circ$ – back to the start. The next rotations are $243^\circ \equiv 3^\circ$, $729^\circ \equiv 9^\circ$, $2187^\circ \equiv 27^\circ$, $6561^\circ \equiv 81^\circ \pmod{120^\circ}$ (each $3^{n+4} - 3^n = 80\cdot 3^n$ is a multiple of 120 because $3^n$ is a multiple of 3 for $n\ge1$), so the pattern repeats.

Positions: $0^\circ, 3^\circ, 12^\circ, 39^\circ$ – four different ones.

**Answer: (B) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-30.title: Chessboard colouring
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0708-30.body:
Colour the board like a chessboard with the corners black: 13 black and 12 white cells. Every jump goes to a cell of the other colour. So the kangaroos from black cells land on white cells and vice versa. Number rows and columns 1–5.

**At least 5 white cells get kangaroos.** The four corner kangaroos each have only two possible target cells, and these four pairs are different: the corner (1,1) can go to (1,2) or (2,1), the corner (1,5) to (1,4) or (2,5), and so on. The kangaroo from the centre (3,3) can only go to (2,3), (3,2), (3,4), (4,3), none of which is next to a corner. So at least 5 different white cells are occupied.

**At least 4 black cells get kangaroos.** The white cells (1,2), (2,5), (5,4), (4,1) have neighbours $\{(1,1),(1,3),(2,2)\}$, $\{(1,5),(3,5),(2,4)\}$, $\{(5,5),(5,3),(4,4)\}$, $\{(5,1),(3,1),(4,2)\}$ – four disjoint sets. So their four kangaroos land on four different black cells.

Hence at least 9 cells are occupied and at most $25 - 9 = 16$ are empty.

**16 is possible:** let all black-cell kangaroos jump to the white cells (1,2), (1,4), (3,2), (4,5), (5,2) and all white-cell kangaroos jump to the black cells (1,1), (2,4), (4,2), (4,4). (Every black cell is next to one of those five white cells, and every white cell is next to one of those four black cells.) Then only 9 cells are occupied.

**Answer: (D) 16**
